This strategy acknowledges the high competition for y and x, and attempts to leverage my higher priority at w compared to others. It also allows me to pursue my second choice (z) if my first (x) doesn't work out.

Therefore, I'm going to adjust my ranking based on the information about other applicants’ preferences. I believe that prioritizing x over z will increase my chances of getting matched to a school I like.
